The term “hot takes” is bad branding and should be replaced with “big brain beliefs.” 

(I’m not sure if we are supposed to explain our hot takes or not, so if not, please ignore this parenthetical statement: 

The best hot takes are the ones that express unconventional thinking but actually make you reconsider how you look at something. In everyday conversation, people say “oh that’s a hot take” in response to something outlandish and/or offensive. This has the potential to be problematic and lazy. Asking for brain beliefs inspires people to look deeper into the world around them and share their unique insight to improve the lives of others around them.)

When it comes to vacation locations, beach vacations are the worst. Sand is probably the worst substance in all of nature. It is essentially nature’s glitter. It gets everywhere and into every nook and cranny of your body and belongings. The salt water from the ocean only makes the stickiness of the sands even worse. Plus, when it gets in your eyes, you can’t rub your eyes to ease the burn because: sand. There are also a lot of things that make a beach vacation miserable: windy days make umbrellas unusable, laying a towel down impossible, and blowing up more sand. Other thing: jellyfish, sharks, seaweed, red tide, strong currents, rainy days, overcast days.
